name: Avalanche-White Salmon Glaciers
descent_text: Climb out onto the summit plateau and head for the true summit, then descend the South Spur: cross the crater rim past Pikers Peak and follow the broad snow slopes of Crescent Ridge down to the Lunch Counter flats, where glissading is common on soft snow. From there the South Climb Trail runs down the old roadbed to Cold Springs, so no shuttle is needed if you started there. Going back down the White Salmon and Avalanche Glaciers is possible in good snow but means a short, steep 45-degree entry below the summit saddle and crevasses that open on the northern and western parts of the glacier by midsummer. Carry an axe and rope team for either descent.
approach: Start at the Cold Springs trailhead (about 5,600 ft) at the end of FR 8040 and walk the South Climb Trail up the old roadbed to its junction with the Round the Mountain Trail near 6,200 ft. Turn right (northwest) onto the Round the Mountain Trail and follow its up-and-down traverse for roughly two miles, much of it under snow in early season, to the stream draining the Avalanche Glacier basin near 6,100 ft. Follow the stream and the moraines above it to the moraine-filled bowl at about 7,200 ft, where the Avalanche Glacier route and the Southwest Chutes meet. The glacier begins above this bowl, and a camp here shortens the summit day.
overview: Approach via the PCT or the Shorthorn trail. Under normal conditions, climb the glacier on its right side. Parties go in late spring; expect mostly moderate to steep snow, sometimes with a headwall of alpine ice. Simul-climbing works for most of it, and pickets with a running belay give protection if needed. Descend by the south side or the neighboring snowfield.
